summary: Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count backward by ones from 20.
Write numerals 0 to 20 and use one to show how many objects (0 for none).
Count objects one-to-one, know the last number is the total, and next is one more, previous one less.
Solve addition and subtraction story problems within 10 using objects or drawings.
Break numbers up to 10 into two parts in more than one way.
For a number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 with it.
Add and subtract within 5 fluently.
Sort objects into categories, count each category, and order categories by count (up to 10).
Name shapes correctly whatever their size or orientation.
Compare flat and solid shapes, describing how they are alike and different.
Put simple shapes together to make squares, rectangles and hexagons.
Solve all types of addition and subtraction story problems within 20, unknown in any position.
Add and subtract within 20, fluent within 10, using counting on and making ten.
Know what the equal sign means and decide if addition/subtraction equations are true or false.
Count forward and backward from any number below 120; read and write numerals to 120.
Know the two digits of a two-digit number are tens and ones, including teens and decades.
Add within 100 (two-digit plus one-digit or a multiple of 10) with models and place value.
Tell and write time to the hour and half hour on analog and digital clocks.
Identify pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters by their value.
Tell defining from non-defining shape attributes; build and draw shapes with given attributes.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more shares means smaller shares.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction story problems within 100.
Add and subtract within 20 fluently; know all sums of two one-digit numbers by end of grade 2.
Know the digits of a three-digit number are hundreds, tens and ones, including 100 as ten tens.
Break a three-digit number into hundreds, tens and ones in several ways, like 4 hundreds 12 tens.
Compare three-digit numbers by place value using words and >, =, <.
Add and subtract within 100 with place-value strategies; the word fluently is left out.
Add and subtract within 1,000 with models and place value, regrouping when needed.
Measure length by choosing and using rulers, yardsticks, meter sticks or tapes.
Tell and write time to the nearest five minutes with a.m. and p.m.
Solve money story problems up to $10 with bills and coins, using $ and cent signs.
Split a rectangle into rows and columns of equal squares and count them.
Split circles and rectangles into halves, thirds or fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Multiply and divide within 100 fluently; know all one-digit products by end of grade 3.
Solve two-step word problems with the four operations, write equations, check with estimation.
Add and subtract within 1,000 fluently using place-value strategies and algorithms.
Understand unit fractions 1/b and fractions a/b as a copies of 1/b.
Place fractions on a number line by splitting 0 to 1 into equal parts.
Find simple equivalent fractions, write wholes as fractions, compare same-numerator or same-denominator fractions.
Measure lengths to the half and quarter inch and show the data on a line plot.
Link rectangle area to multiplication and the distributive property; area of combined rectangles left out.
Sort quadrilaterals such as rhombuses, rectangles and squares by their attributes.
Solve multi-step whole-number word problems, interpret remainders, and check with estimation.
Read, write and compare multi-digit numbers in numerals, words and expanded form.
Round multi-digit whole numbers to any place.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two digits by two digits, explaining with models.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders, explaining with models.
Explain and make equivalent fractions using visual models.
Compare fractions with unlike numerators and denominators using common parts or benchmarks.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, including word problems.
Compare and order decimals to hundredths using models and >, =, <.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles in real and math problems.
Find unknown angles in diagrams by adding or subtracting angle measures.
Classify flat shapes by parallel or perpendicular lines and angle types; identify right triangles.
Use and evaluate expressions with parentheses, brackets or braces.
Write simple expressions from calculations and interpret them without evaluating.
A digit is worth 10 times the place to its right and 1/10 the place to its left.
Explain zero and decimal-point patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals to hundredths with models and strategies.
Solve fraction addition and subtraction word problems with unlike denominators and estimate.
See a fraction as division and solve division problems with fraction answers.
Solve real problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, including word problems.
Find rectangular prism volume by multiplying or with V = lwh or Bh; combined solids left out.
Plot and interpret points in the first quadrant for real and math situations.

state_code: # - 2023 Mathematics WYCPS (Emended Feb. 2025), effective July 17, 2024, full implementation 2025-26 (the current reduced edition):
# - Ch. 10 Rules on Standards (revised Feb 27, 2025; incorporates the PDF above by reference):
# - WDE fact sheet (SBE reduced the number of standards; standard text not edited): https://edu.wyoming.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/WYCPS-Fact-Sheet.pdf
# - Cross-check: "All Currently-Adopted Grade 1 Standards" lists the same reduced grade 1 set:
# - No official WY-to-CCSS crosswalk found (the WDE resources site needs a login). WY keeps CCSS domain and standard numbers, so the
#   mapping is by number plus a reading of each standard against CCSS text.
# - Grade.Domain.Number with a lowercase sub-letter, e.g. K.CC.1b, 1.MD.3a, 2.NBT.1c. No cluster letter. Numbers follow CCSS numbering, so gaps
#   mark trimmed standards. 1.MD.3a/3b have no parent 1.MD.3 text. The 2023 draft (SBE 2.24.23) printed 1.MD.3 with A/B bullets.
# - Sub-letters that only restate CCSS sub-parts are folded into the parent row: K.CC.4, 1.NBT.1/2/4, 1.G.3, 2.NBT.1 (a-b), 2.NBT.7, 2.G.3,
# - Each standard also has a "Proficient student is able to..." PLD (the performance standard) that repeats the standard; not included.
# CCSS K-5 STANDARDS DROPPED (not covered by any current WY K-5 standard; the Feb 2025 reduction cut ~half of each grade):
# - K: K.CC.A.2 K.CC.B.5 K.CC.C.6 K.CC.C.7 K.OA.A.1 K.NBT.A.1 K.MD.A.1 K.MD.A.2 K.G.A.1 K.G.A.3 K.G.B.5
# - New: count backward by ones from 20 in K (K.CC.1b); count backward within 120 in grade 1 (inside 1.NBT.1a).
# - Moved earlier: identify coins by value in grade 1 (1.MD.3b; CCSS money is 2.MD.C.8).
# - Added: 2.NBT.1c decomposing three-digit numbers in multiple ways; 2.MD.8 caps money problems at $10; K.CC.4c adds "one less".
# - Narrowed: 3.MD.7 drops CCSS 3.MD.C.7d (rectilinear figures); 5.MD.5 drops 5.MD.C.5c (additive volume); 4.MD.7 keeps only the
#   unknown-angle problems; 2.NBT.5 drops "fluently"; K.G.6 names the target shapes (squares, rectangles, hexagons).
# - Limits in cluster headings: grade 3 fractions denominators 2,3,4,6,8; grade 4 fractions 2,3,4,5,6,8,10,12,100; grade 4 whole numbers
#   to 1,000,000. 3.OA.8 says to apply order of operations when no parentheses (CCSS has this as a footnote).
# - K.CC.4 PLD says counting objects "in a range from 10 to 39", which differs from CCSS (to 20); row follows the content standard text.
# - 1.MD.3b marked moved (2.MD.C.8) since CCSS has no coin identification before grade 2; could be read as new.
# - 2.NBT.1c mapped to 2.NBT.A.1 and 2.NBT.B.7 (regrouping) as edited; CCSS has no standalone multiple-decomposition standard.
# - "Edited" calls on small changes (2.MD.8 $10 cap, 2.NBT.5 no fluency, 4.MD.7, K.G.6) are judgment calls; they could be read as same.
# - kind is judged on content: same = CCSS content with only rewording or small example changes.
